title: Vande Bharat Drone Video Captures Jharkhand's Hills Looking Like Switzerland
excerpt: A viral aerial clip shows the saffron-and-grey Vande Bharat Express threading through dense forests and rolling hills on the Barkakana–Ranchi line, prompting viewers to compare India's heartland with the Swiss Alps.
body:
• A drone video of the Vande Bharat Express winding through Jharkhand's forests and hills has gone viral, with viewers likening the landscape to Switzerland.
  • The clip was filmed along the Barkakana–Ranchi railway corridor in the Chota Nagpur region, served by the Patna–Ranchi Vande Bharat Express (22349/22350) since June 2023.
  • It follows a pattern of viral rail-aerial clips — including the Western Ghats "orange snake" video shared by Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw.
  • Jharkhand's tourism sector stands to benefit as the footage spotlights the state's forested hills, valleys and waterfalls.

The Viral Moment

A drone video showing the Vande Bharat Express snaking through lush forests and scenic hills in Jharkhand has taken social media by storm, with thousands of viewers remarking that the landscape looks less like central India and more like the Swiss countryside. The clip, posted to YouTube in mid-September 2026 under the title "Vande Bharat through the green heart of Jharkhand," films the train from above as it runs along the Barkakana–Ranchi railway line — a stretch that cuts through some of the most densely forested rail terrain in the Chota Nagpur plateau region.

From the drone's vantage point, the saffron-and-grey train looks small against an unbroken canopy of green, the track curving through valleys and hillsides that glow in the monsoon light. The footage captures the essence of why these aerial rail videos keep going viral: modern Indian engineering framed by terrain that many viewers simply did not associate with Jharkhand, a state more often in the headlines for its mines and industry than its scenery.

Context & Background

The corridor in the video is served by the Patna–Ranchi Vande Bharat Express (train numbers 22349/22350), India's 20th Vande Bharat service, flagged off by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on June 27, 2023. The mini Vande Bharat 2.0 rake — built at the Integral Coach Factory in Perambur, Chennai, under the Make in India initiative — covers 379 km in about six hours, running six days a week with halts at Jehanabad, Gaya, Koderma, Hazaribagh Town, Barkakana and Mesra before reaching Ranchi.

The engineering beneath the scenery is substantial. The new Ranchi–Koderma alignment via Barkakana, which the route uses, threads a 27-km stretch between Sidhwar in Ramgarh and Sanki in Ranchi that includes four tunnels — the longest 1.7 km — alongside multiple bridges and curves carved through the plateau. During trial runs in June 2023, the train completed the Patna–Ranchi run in under six hours, arriving ahead of schedule.

The Jharkhand clip is not an isolated phenomenon. Earlier this year, a dramatic FPV-drone video of a saffron Vande Bharat winding through the mist-covered Western Ghats on the Sakleshpur–Subrahmanya Road section — a route with 57 tunnels, 258 bridges and 108 sharp curves — went viral after Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw shared it, with viewers comparing the train to a "giant orange snake" gliding through a sea of green. Another widely shared clip showed a Vande Bharat gliding across the Chenab rail bridge, the world's highest railway arch bridge at 359 metres, floating through clouds above Jammu and Kashmir.

Impact & Analysis

These aerial clips function as inadvertent tourism campaigns. Jharkhand, home to Netarhat — often called the "Queen of Chotanagpur" — the waterfalls of Hundru, Jonha and Dassam, and the forests of Betla National Park, has long struggled to convert its natural assets into a tourism identity. A single viral drone video can do in days what a state tourism board campaign takes months to achieve: reframe perception.

The timing matters. Post-monsoon is when the Chota Nagpur plateau is at its greenest, and September–October is the start of the domestic travel season building toward Diwali. Indian Railways has also leaned into this kind of content — the Railways ministry routinely amplifies the most striking rail footage on its official handles — because each viral clip doubles as proof-of-concept for the Vande Bharat programme's reach into terrain once considered difficult to serve.

There is a commercial layer too. The Barkakana–Ranchi stretch is not merely scenic; it connects Ranchi to the industrial and coal belts of Ramgarh and Dhanbad, and onward to Patna, making it a genuine commuter and business corridor dressed in cinematic landscapes.

Diaspora Angle

For the Jharkhandi and Bihari diaspora — concentrated in the US, the Gulf and the UK — the clip lands differently than a generic travel video. Many in the diaspora left a Jharkhand defined by mining towns and industrial outposts; seeing the state's forests rendered in drone-shot splendour reframes the idea of "home" they carry abroad. Videos like this routinely circulate in diaspora WhatsApp groups and community pages, and they shape trip planning: the window-seat view from Ranchi toward Barkakana is now, thanks to a drone, part of the visual vocabulary of the region.

What's Next

Expect Jharkhand's tourism department to move quickly — the state has previously piggybacked on viral moments to push destinations like Patratu Valley and Netarhat. The bigger question is whether Indian Railways formalises what is currently accidental: curated "scenic rail" marketing for its most photogenic corridors, the way Switzerland's own railways have built an entire tourism industry around the Glacier Express. The drone has done the scouting; the packaging is the next step.
image_caption: A Vande Bharat Express train photographed near Mumbai. The viral drone video that sparked comparisons with Switzerland was filmed on the Barkakana–Ranchi line in Jharkhand.
